text: A museum digitisation project may face a scanner delivery delay. A team member also reports a possible licensing restriction. Neither has happened. What should the team do to decide which needs attention first?

options.text: Handle whichever concern was reported first.
Record both and assess their likelihood and potential effect on the project.
Treat both as confirmed delays and move the deadline immediately.
Wait until one happens before discussing it.

text: A remote research project depends on one transport route that may close. The team has already judged the threat significant. Which response plan is most actionable?

options.text: Ask everyone to be careful and leave ownership open.
Remove the threat from the register once it is discussed.
Assign an owner, agree on warning signs and arrange a feasible alternative route.
Promise stakeholders that the route will never close.

text: A team arranged a backup supplier, but the supplier has now changed its delivery conditions. What should happen to the existing risk plan?

options.text: Reassess the exposure, check the response and update the register and actions.
Keep it unchanged because a response was already approved.
Close the risk because two suppliers have been contacted.
Wait until project closure to review the change.
